title: Median consensus for 1-10 response ratings
scenario: Rushed and superseded submissions are dropped, each item's consensus is a median after a single outlier pass, low-agreement items are escalated and expert adjudications override; the summary reports status counts, escalations and per-category means.

verified.why_correct: `int(float(text))` looks like it silently truncates, but the README says ratings are whole numbers sometimes written as `6.0`, so float-then-int is exactly what is needed; blanks and out-of-range values return None.
`<= 1` looks like it should be `< 1`, but the spec counts ratings within 1 point inclusive. It divides by the number of remaining ratings and rounds to 3 decimals as required.

bugs.title: Duration read with timedelta.seconds
bugs.symptom: Test 1 test_1_rushed_counts: ann-07 shows 1 rushed submission ({'ann-07': 1, 'ann-08': 1, 'ann-10': 1} instead of {'ann-08': 1, 'ann-10': 1}). I-09's consensus and status do not change.
bugs.why: `.seconds` is only the seconds component of the timedelta, ignoring whole days. s-040 was open for 1 day and 12 seconds, so it reads as 12 seconds and is dropped as rushed.
hints: ann-07 is counted as rushed. Find their submissions and compute each duration.
Look at how a submission's duration is measured.
probes: Why didn't dropping s-040 change I-09's consensus or status?
What does timedelta(days=1, seconds=12).seconds return, and why?

bugs.title: Resubmissions deduped by submission id
bugs.symptom: Test 1 test_2_resubmitted_item: I-04 has agreement 0.8 instead of 1.0; status 'agreed' and consensus 7 are unchanged.
bugs.why: Submission ids are unique, so keying on them never collapses anything. ann-01's superseded 5 on I-04 stays alongside their later 7, which drops I-04's agreement to 0.8.
hints: I-04 has five counted ratings. How many annotators rated it?
Look at what latest_only uses to recognise the same submission twice.
probes: Why did I-04's consensus stay 7 even with the extra rating?
Which other field of the report would show ann-01's extra rating?

bugs.title: Even-count median uses floor division
bugs.symptom: Test 2 test_3_consensus_values: I-06's consensus is 6 instead of 6.5. Every other item matches.
bugs.why: With integer ratings, `//` floors the mean of the two middle values, so I-06 (6, 6, 7, 7) gets 6 instead of 6.5. Items whose middle pair has an even sum look fine.
hints: Only I-06 is off, by exactly 0.5. What is special about its ratings?
Look at the even-length branch of median().
probes: Why were I-02, I-04 and I-09 right even though they also have an even number of ratings?
Why did I-06's status not change?

bugs.title: Outliers removed while iterating the same list
bugs.symptom: Test 2 test_4_outlier_counts: ann-05 is missing ({'ann-03': 1, 'ann-04': 1} instead of also 'ann-05': 1). I-08's consensus is still 8.
bugs.why: Removing from the list being iterated shifts the next element into the current index, so the loop skips it. On I-08 the 2 and the 1 are adjacent; once the 2 is removed the 1 is never examined.
hints: ann-05's 1 on I-08 is 7 points from the median. Why isn't it an outlier?
Look at how drop_outliers walks and edits the list.
Iterate over a copy: `for r in list(kept):`.
probes: Why did I-07's single outlier still get removed?
Why did I-08's consensus stay 8 even with the 1 left in?

bugs.title: Category total not reset per category
bugs.symptom: Test 3 test_5_category_means: writing is 18.83 instead of 6.67; coding (5.67) is right.
bugs.why: The running total is created once, so each category's sum includes every category before it. coding (first) is right, writing includes coding and math.
hints: coding is right but writing is far too high. What comes between them?
Where is the running total initialised in category_means?
probes: Why is the first category always right with this mistake?
How would `sum(values) / len(values)` have avoided it?

bugs.title: Enum status compared to a string
bugs.symptom: Test 3 test_6_escalated_items: escalated is [] instead of ['I-02', 'I-10'], even though status_counts reports 2 escalated items.
bugs.why: `res.status` is a Status enum member, and a plain Enum never equals its value string, so nothing matches and the list is empty. status_counts works because it uses `.value`.
hints: status_counts says 2 escalated, but the escalated list is empty.
Compare how summarize builds status_counts and escalated.
probes: Would `class Status(str, Enum)` have made the comparison work? Why?
Why does no error get raised?

context_qa.q: What happens in build_report(), step by step?
context_qa.a: It loads the registry and items, reads ratings (dropping blanks, out-of-range values and unknown annotators), splits off rushed submissions with split_rushed, keeps one submission per key with latest_only, then score_items builds the per-item results and the list of outlier ratings. Counters over the remaining ratings and the outliers feed the annotators table, and summarize builds the summary.
A list of the submissions whose duration_seconds is at least MIN_SECONDS (20), and a Counter of annotator id → number of submissions under that.

context_qa.q: How does latest_only choose between two submissions with the same key?
context_qa.a: It keeps the stored one unless the new one's finished_at is greater than or equal to it, so the latest wins and a later row wins a tie. The output is in first-seen key order.

context_qa.q: In score_items, which check runs first: adjudication or the minimum count?
context_qa.a: Adjudication. An item with adjudicated_rating set is marked ADJUDICATED with that consensus before the MIN_RATINGS (3) check runs.

context_qa.q: What does drop_outliers compare each rating against?
context_qa.a: The median of all the item's counted ratings, computed once before the loop; ratings more than OUTLIER_GAP (3) away are moved to the outliers list.

context_qa.q: What type is ItemResult.status, and how does it reach the report?
context_qa.a: It is a `Status` member (a plain Enum). The report's items section and status_counts convert it with `.value`.
Every item whose consensus is not None, including adjudicated ones, grouped by the item's category from items.csv.
